To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
farmers prefer conventional production systems to alternative systems with a higher level of animal welfare.

Dutch broiler and fatening pig farmers preferred conventional production systems over free-range systems, and that they were not motivated to switch to a production system with higher animal-welfare standards.
Dutch broiler and pork farmers generally have negative preferences towards alternative practices.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the identification of the factors that influence the decision making of farmers to adopt a production system with higher animal standards, and the identification of farmers’ preferences towards animal welfare.
the development of methods to support the decision-making process of farmers in the field of animal welfare.
the question whether farmers are intrinsically motivated towards animal welfare.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the majority of farmers in this study were not intrinsicaly motivated to convert to higher animal welfare systems, but that they would be willing to do so if they were to receive financial compensation for the higher costs involved.
the results of this study are inconclusive, as the results of the conjoint analysis are not supported by the cluster analysis.

farmers are not motivated to convert to an alternative production system with higher animal-welfare standards and therefore, the level of AW on-farm will be determined by other factors than intrinsic motivation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the trustworthiness of the results could be increased by mixing different methods, such as conjoint analysis with focus groups and/or interviews.
a mixed method is needed to enhance the trustworthiness of the results.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of different methods can help to enhance the trustworthiness, quality and applicability of the results.
by combining multiple methods, such as conjoint analysis and cluster analysis, the trustworthiness, quality, and usefulness of results can be improved.
mixing different methods to elicit farmers’ preferences can be a powerful tool to enhance trustworthiness and the quality of results.
